hypotheses.title: Config migration/default insertion is silent, where pinned prints what it changed
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Run the shipped binary over a config.yaml carrying one legacy key and one missing default; capture stdout; diff against a pinned boot on the same copy. Then port the two console.log lines and the creation warning with a recorded fixture.
hypotheses.counterargument: GOAL.md 15.5 wants a quiet default and internal/app/startup_trace.go:25-30 made stage timings opt-in; if the owners decide pinned's config-init messages are non-contract this closes as intentional-parity. Today AGENTS rule 13 says reproduce config creation/key migration/default insertion without naming the observable.

hypotheses.title: Legacy user-data migration announces a single line where pinned warns for ten seconds and offers cancellation
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Boot both subjects on a tree with public/characters present; capture stdout during the ten-second pause and compare line count and content. The adversarial case boot.legacy-migration-cost measures only that the pause is 10s once and announced; extend it to compare the announcement shape.
hypotheses.counterargument: internal/adversarial/violations.golden records the deliberate correction: the pause is pinned's warning period and the invariant is 'announced before spent'. One line satisfies the letter of that invariant; the residual complaint is the missing countdown/cancel prompt, which the ratchet does not measure.

hypotheses.title: gotavern migrate --force backs up only config.yaml and data/; certs and the global extension overlay are truncated in place
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Pre-create <dest>/certs/server.pem with distinct bytes and no config.yaml/data; run gotavern migrate --from <src> --dest <dest>; assert the pre-existing cert bytes are unchanged (today they are overwritten). Then add certs and the overlay path to Conflicts and to the force-backup loop and re-run.
hypotheses.counterargument: The destination shape (certs/overlay without config+data) is unusual and the command is GoTavern product behaviour, not pinned parity, so fixing it costs no compatibility; the likelihood is low but the overwrite is silent and forbidden by AGENTS rule 28.

hypotheses.title: The two recursive destructive routes run outside the shared content lock
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Fire a chat save (which holds the content lock) concurrently with POST /api/users/reset-step2 on both subjects; compare the surviving tree for a file recreated inside a tree the user asked to empty. Repeat with SIGKILL between RemoveAll and EnsureDirectories.
hypotheses.counterargument: Pinned's fsPromises.rm is async on a single event loop, so a concurrent request can interleave there too; taking the lock could be 'safer but different'. The row is confirmed only if the two subjects produce different surviving trees; if they do not, record it as intentional-parity and keep the crash probe.

hypotheses.title: Swallowed card-write errors make characters/create answer 200 with no card, and this is pinned parity
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: chmod the characters/ directory read-only, POST /api/characters/create on both subjects, assert status 200 and the file absent on both; that is the discriminating parity capture. A later product decision may change it, but the parity capture comes first.
hypotheses.counterargument: This is inherited behaviour; changing it breaks drop-in parity (AGENTS boundary 5). The audit value is that no gate says the route can claim success with nothing written, so a user who loses a card has no error to point at.

hypotheses.title: gotavern migrate writes the destination config.yaml non-atomically
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Kill the process during copyConfig on a large source; observe a truncated destination config, then a second run refusing as a conflict. Replace os.WriteFile with a temp+fsync+rename and re-run.
hypotheses.counterargument: Destination-only, recoverable with --force, and the plan is printed before writing; but it is a write-file-atomic-shaped gap in a tree that owns atomicReplace.

hypotheses.title: Tokenizer cache files are written non-atomically and a corrupt cache is not detected at read time
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Truncate a cached <model>.json, request a tokenizer route, assert a fallback/rebuild rather than a wrong count; then kill during materialisation and assert the cache is complete or absent.
hypotheses.counterargument: Pinned writes the cache the same way, so a mismatch would be a parity question; the cache is derived and deletable.

hypotheses.title: The character disk-cache directory is created and verified but cache records are never written
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Boot both subjects with performance.useDiskCache true on a tree with cards; compare _cache/characters entry counts and whether pinned writes records here.
hypotheses.counterargument: GOAL.md already classifies the character disk cache as a derived, rebuildable parity/performance gap; nothing user-owned depends on it. What is still unrecorded is that the DIRECTORY exists-but-empty on the Go side.

hypotheses.title: Image and avatar uploads take no lock while every JSON write does
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Concurrent overwrite of the same image name from two requests; assert readers never see a torn file (atomicReplace guarantees it) and that last-writer-wins is the only outcome. Record the result so 'no lock' is not read as 'not atomic'.
hypotheses.counterargument: The content lock protects read-modify-write sequences, not single replacements; adding it would only add contention.

hypotheses.title: Extension move is copy-then-delete with no staging
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: SIGKILL during the copy of a large extension; assert the source is intact and the destination partial, then that a retry answers 409. Record the inherited failure mode; a staging fix would be a deliberate divergence from pinned cpSync+rmSync.
hypotheses.counterargument: The user's source directory is intact after the crash, the state is recoverable by deleting the partial destination, and matching pinned is required.

questions: Does pinned's config-init console output (creation warning, added-key list, migrated-key list, Using config path) count as contract for B-H1? GOAL.md 15.5 and AGENTS 13 point opposite ways; the Lead/owner must decide and, if it counts, a stdout port with a recorded fixture closes it.

Is a pristine pre-boot copy byte-identical after a boot? No test copies a tree, boots, then re-hashes the copy. GOAL.md section 14 item 4 needs that; it is a scenario-design question for Lane E (the long-lived fixture has the copy but does not re-hash it after the journey).

Does any GoTavern code read <dataRoot>/_cache/characters? The directory is created/verified (S13) but no reader or writer of cache records was found by grepping internal/ for _cache; confirming the negative needs the Lead's source graph rather than a bounded grep.
Is Go's atomic restore-snapshot (W03) acceptable parity given pinned deletes settings.json before copying? Safer and unobservable except across a crash; parity policy, not filesystem behaviour.
Cross-user contention on the single data-root content lock is Lane C's question; this lane records only that the lock is data-root-scoped and that every JSON writer depends on it.
